files.title: Principles
files.description: Source-backed reasoning rules extracted from Modules 1–10 of the marketing course.

files.title: A segmentation is a map, not the market
files.description: Segment populations and values are evidence-based approximations that should be directionally sound, updated regularly, and not presented with false precision.
headings: A segmentation is a map, not the market

files.title: Align marketing and sales targeting choices
files.description: Marketing and sales should compare their target choices and agree how their activities support one another.
headings: Align marketing and sales targeting choices

files.title: Brand building and activation should work together without forcing both into one execution
files.description: Long-term brand building creates future demand for activation to harvest, but separate executions usually preserve each job more effectively than a double-duty advertisement.
headings: Brand building and activation should work together without forcing both into one execution

files.title: Brand codes should be few, stable, and consistently applied
files.description: A small selected palette becomes distinctive through long-term, consistent use across relevant customer touchpoints.
headings: Brand codes should be few, stable, and consistently applied

files.title: Brand-specific code evidence can override category averages
files.description: Average performance by code type should not displace evidence that a particular code is strongly associated with a specific brand.
headings: Brand-specific code evidence can override category averages

files.title: Channel breadth must not outrun viable investment
files.description: Adding channels can improve effectiveness only when the budget can fund each selected medium at a useful level.
headings: Channel breadth must not outrun viable investment

files.title: Channel management depends on interdependent partners
files.description: Distribution performance depends on firms recognising their mutual dependence and sustaining workable roles and returns across the channel.
headings: Channel management depends on interdependent partners

files.title: Choose positioning associations by fit, not hierarchy
files.description: Features, benefits, category entry points, emotional associations, and purpose are options to combine by fit rather than a universal ranking.
headings: Choose positioning associations by fit, not hierarchy

files.title: Clients should provide strategy and preserve agency creative autonomy
files.description: Clients should define the strategic platform and constraints while leaving creative approaches and tactical ideas to the agency.
headings: Clients should provide strategy and preserve agency creative autonomy

files.title: Co-branding works through complementary association transfer
files.description: A strong co-brand combines complementary capabilities and associations that customers can credibly attribute to the joint offer.
headings: Co-branding works through complementary association transfer

files.title: Communications effectiveness comes from an interacting system, not one lever
files.description: Briefing, budget, long- and short-term roles, media, integration, codes, creative, emotion, testing, longevity, and measurement reinforce one another.
headings: Communications effectiveness comes from an interacting system, not one lever

files.title: Communications investment and expected return must move together
files.description: A reduced communications investment requires a revised return expectation rather than preserving the original forecast.
headings: Communications investment and expected return must move together

files.title: Communications should be measured at campaign level and used to improve
files.description: Campaign performance should be judged against its own objectives and evidence, then used to refine creative and media choices.
headings: Communications should be measured at campaign level and used to improve

files.title: Complementary approaches can outperform either-or choices
files.description: When two approaches perform different useful jobs, a deliberate combination may be stronger than treating them as mutually exclusive.
headings: Complementary approaches can outperform either-or choices

files.title: Complementary channels can create more-than-additive effects
files.description: A deliberate mix of channels can combine distinct strengths and amplify a campaign beyond concentrating the same investment in one channel.
headings: Complementary channels can create more-than-additive effects

files.title: Complex thinking should produce simple strategy
files.description: Deep analysis should resolve into a clear strategic direction that people can understand and execute.
headings: Complex thinking should produce simple strategy

files.title: Consolidated retail power must be managed, not assumed controllable
files.description: Brands should manage the effects of powerful retailers rather than assume there is a lawful tactic that restores supplier control.
headings: Consolidated retail power must be managed, not assumed controllable

files.title: Customer alternatives define segment-relative competition
files.description: Competition is defined by the alternatives customers consider and can change across customer segments.

files.title: Customer scope extends beyond the immediate buyer
files.description: Market understanding must include the relevant parties between the producer and the person who ultimately consumes or uses the product.
headings: Customer scope extends beyond the immediate buyer

files.title: Customers buy solutions to jobs, not products as defined internally
files.description: Product decisions should begin with the customer's underlying job or need rather than the organisation's category and product definition.
headings: Customers buy solutions to jobs, not products as defined internally

files.title: Differentiation seeks relative advantage, not uniqueness
files.description: A brand can differentiate by being perceived as stronger on a few important attributes without uniquely owning them.
headings: Differentiation seeks relative advantage, not uniqueness

files.title: Direct-channel control does not guarantee scale or profitability
files.description: Direct distribution can improve control, data, and proximity, but those advantages do not prove that a direct-only model can achieve profitable scale.
headings: Direct-channel control does not guarantee scale or profitability

files.title: Discount effects must be judged by profit and source of sales
files.description: A promotional sales uplift should be evaluated through its margin effect and the origin of the additional sales, not treated as wholly incremental demand.
headings: Discount effects must be judged by profit and source of sales

files.title: Discover behavioural groups before using demographics as identifiers
files.description: Form segments from observed attitudes and behaviours first, then test demographic variables as identifiers rather than assuming needs from demographics.
headings: Discover behavioural groups before using demographics as identifiers

files.title: Discover options qualitatively before measuring them
files.description: Quantitative precision cannot repair an incomplete or incorrect set of options; qualitative exploration must establish what should be measured first.
headings: Discover options qualitatively before measuring them

files.title: Distinctiveness is recognition, not competitive superiority
files.description: Distinctiveness concerns whether people can identify a brand as itself; it is separate from relative preference over alternatives.
headings: Distinctiveness is recognition, not competitive superiority

files.title: Do not combine markets when aggregation erases differences
files.description: Use one segmentation across markets only when aggregation preserves useful similarities and does not conceal material country or category differences.
headings: Do not combine markets when aggregation erases differences

files.title: Early distribution should establish the brand before maximising availability
files.description: A new brand should use its earliest channel choices to establish its intended positioning before pursuing broad physical availability.
headings: Early distribution should establish the brand before maximising availability

files.title: Effective campaign platforms should be renewed, not routinely replaced
files.description: Campaign age alone is not evidence of declining effectiveness; proven ideas can be refreshed through new executions and sustained over many years.
headings: Effective campaign platforms should be renewed, not routinely replaced

files.title: Emotional communication can outperform rational persuasion
files.description: Communications should consider the emotional response they seek rather than defaulting to rational explanation as the strongest route to effectiveness.
headings: Emotional communication can outperform rational persuasion

files.title: Evidence-backed value supports holding the price line
files.description: When customer research, strategy, positioning, and product quality support the price, marketers should resist routine discount pressure and preserve the value already created.
headings: Evidence-backed value supports holding the price line

files.title: Existing-customer evidence can refine positioning
files.description: For an existing offer, loyal customers can reveal true alternatives, strengths, and reasons for preference that improve its position.

files.title: Existing products should be continuously improved
files.description: Product work should include systematic improvement of in-market offers, not only the creation of new products.
headings: Existing products should be continuously improved

files.title: Focused entry can support mass-market growth under constraints
files.description: A resource-constrained organisation can begin with a geographic, subcategory, or segment focus while retaining a broader long-term market ambition.
headings: Focused entry can support mass-market growth under constraints

files.title: The funnel base must match the selected target
files.description: The 100 percent population at the top of a funnel must represent the market or segment the strategy actually targets.
headings: The funnel base must match the selected target

files.title: Funnel performance needs conversion and competitive context
files.description: Funnel stages should be interpreted through stage-to-stage conversion and relevant competitor comparisons, not isolated percentages.
headings: Funnel performance needs conversion and competitive context

files.title: Funnels must fit the market and buying process
files.description: A useful funnel is designed for the actual market, offer, and customer decision process rather than copied from a generic model.
headings: Funnels must fit the market and buying process

files.title: Grey-market leakage can become self-reinforcing
files.description: Legal but unauthorised channel leakage can erode distribution discipline and become increasingly difficult to control once products circulate through parallel routes.

files.title: Long-and-short budget allocation must fit the context
files.description: The balance between brand building and activation should reflect the company, category, situation, and current evidence rather than treating 60/40 as a fixed rule.
headings: Long-and-short budget allocation must fit the context

files.title: Long-term brand building and short-term activation require different measures
files.description: Brand-building investment should be assessed through brand outcomes, while activation can be assessed through immediate response and return.
headings: Long-term brand building and short-term activation require different measures

files.title: Map the whole market before choosing targets
files.description: Segmentation is diagnosis: it describes every part of the defined market before targeting chooses which segments to pursue or reject.
headings: Map the whole market before choosing targets

files.title: Market intelligence must circulate, and response is judgement
files.description: Market orientation requires organisation-wide circulation of customer and competitor intelligence, followed by an appropriate response rather than automatic compliance.
headings: Market intelligence must circulate, and response is judgement

files.title: Market orientation must precede market research
files.description: Research is most useful when the marketer is oriented to seek, accept, and act on market evidence.
headings: Market orientation must precede market research

files.title: Marketers are not the consumer
files.description: A marketer must remove personal and producer-side assumptions before interpreting the market.

files.title: Marketing influence does not require control of every P
files.description: Marketers should contribute to product, pricing, communications, and distribution decisions even when other functions retain formal control.
headings: Marketing influence does not require control of every P

files.title: Marketing is broader than advertising and sales
files.description: Marketing can refer to narrow communication and persuasion or to the broader work of listening, understanding, orienting, and shaping the marketing mix.
headings: Marketing is broader than advertising and sales

files.title: Marketing must create value for both customers and the organisation
files.description: Marketing must align value delivered to customers with value retained by the organisation rather than sacrificing either side of the exchange.
headings: Marketing must create value for both customers and the organisation

files.title: Marketing's prime directive is to represent the customer
files.description: Marketing's distinctive organisational responsibility is to bring the customer's perspective into the organisation and keep it connected to the market.
headings: Marketing's prime directive is to represent the customer

files.title: Media delivery cannot compensate for weak creative
files.description: Distribution speed, reach, and channel optimisation cannot rescue an advertisement whose creative content is ineffective.
headings: Media delivery cannot compensate for weak creative

files.title: Media roles are determined by use, not channel label
files.description: A medium becomes brand-building or activation through the campaign's objective and execution rather than through a permanent channel classification.
headings: Media roles are determined by use, not channel label

files.title: Non-targeting is temporary non-investment, not exclusion
files.description: Not targeting a customer group means withholding focused resources for a defined period, not refusing its business permanently.
headings: Non-targeting is temporary non-investment, not exclusion

files.title: NPS is a contextual learning measure, not a growth predictor
files.description: Net Promoter Score should be interpreted against relevant benchmarks and customer explanations, not treated as a universal predictor of growth.
headings: NPS is a contextual learning measure, not a growth predictor

files.title: Objective changes can require new tactics
files.description: A changed objective can require different tactical execution even when the target market and intended position remain stable.
headings: Objective changes can require new tactics

files.title: Objective count is a team-level limit
files.description: A team should hold only a small handful of objectives across its products and segments, rather than assigning a full set to each one.
headings: Objective count is a team-level limit

files.title: Objective targets must balance ambition and realism
files.description: An objective should stretch performance enough to matter while remaining credible enough to guide plans and budgets.
headings: Objective targets must balance ambition and realism

files.title: Objectives should follow funnel diagnosis
files.description: Marketing objectives should be selected from a populated funnel rather than inferred from isolated sales outcomes.

files.title: Omnichannel quality depends on integration, not channel count
files.description: Omnichannel maturity comes from a seamless experience and connected customer data across priority channels, not from operating the largest possible number of channels.
headings: Omnichannel quality depends on integration, not channel count

files.title: Positioning is internal strategy expressed through touchpoints
files.description: Customers experience positioning through coordinated tactical choices and touchpoints, not through the internal positioning document itself.
headings: Positioning is internal strategy expressed through touchpoints

files.title: Positioning must use customer data, not internal opinion
files.description: Positioning choices should be grounded in customer evidence about purchase drivers, alternatives, and perceptions.
headings: Positioning must use customer data, not internal opinion

files.title: Positioning promises must be deliverable
files.description: A brand should position only on promises the organisation already has the competence and capability to deliver.

files.title: Positioning works backwards from intended customer associations
files.description: Positioning should begin with what the target customer should think about the brand, then express that intended association compactly.
headings: Positioning works backwards from intended customer associations

files.title: Price increases should be communicated candidly and with value context
files.description: A price increase should be named directly, announced with adequate notice, explained, and accompanied by a reminder of the offer's continuing value.
headings: Price increases should be communicated candidly and with value context

files.title: Price presentation shapes perceived value and demand
files.description: How a price is framed, anchored, and presented can change perceived value and customer choice even when the underlying offer or nominal difference is unchanged.
headings: Price presentation shapes perceived value and demand

files.title: Price should follow customer perceived value, not cost-plus arithmetic
files.description: Costs establish a floor, while customer perceived value should guide the price; a markup applied to cost is not a substitute for market evidence.
headings: Price should follow customer perceived value, not cost-plus arithmetic

files.title: Pricing decisions require customer evidence, not internal intuition
files.description: Price setting should use evidence about customer value and behaviour rather than inherited assumptions, competitor imitation, or unsupported managerial judgement.
headings: Pricing decisions require customer evidence, not internal intuition

files.title: Pricing is the revenue-producing element of the marketing mix
files.description: Pricing is distinctive among the four Ps because it returns value from willing customers to the organisation as revenue.
headings: Pricing is the revenue-producing element of the marketing mix

files.title: Pricing power combines value perception with the ability to hold price
files.description: A business has pricing power when customer perceptions support a higher price and the organisation can raise or maintain that price without losing the business.
headings: Pricing power combines value perception with the ability to hold price

files.title: Product expansion must be balanced with rationalisation
files.description: Portfolio growth should be counterbalanced by removing weak products so resources and attention remain concentrated.
headings: Product expansion must be balanced with rationalisation

files.title: Product success requires quality and market preparation
files.description: A strong product is necessary but insufficient; organisations must also prepare the market and communicate the product's value.
headings: Product success requires quality and market preparation

files.title: Profit, not revenue, is the primary commercial test
files.description: Revenue should be evaluated by the profit it carries because higher sales or turnover can coexist with weaker margins and lower profitability.
headings: Profit, not revenue, is the primary commercial test

files.title: Qualitative depth does not establish population magnitude
files.description: Focus groups and ethnography provide depth and qualities, but small qualitative samples do not establish how common a finding is across the market.
headings: Qualitative depth does not establish population magnitude

files.title: Quantitative extrapolation requires a representative sample
files.description: A survey result can represent a wider market only when its sample covers the relevant consumer types and is sufficiently robust for the intended population.
headings: Quantitative extrapolation requires a representative sample

files.title: Record cross-segment influence only when the relationship is specific
files.description: Show spillover between segments only when a credible, directional relationship identifies how one segment influences another.
headings: Record cross-segment influence only when the relationship is specific

files.title: Repeated discounting can become a self-reinforcing strategic trap
files.description: Promotions can pull demand forward, train customers and organisations to expect further discounts, intensify price competition, and conceal unresolved strategic problems.
headings: Repeated discounting can become a self-reinforcing strategic trap

files.title: Research methods are trade-offs, not a ranking
files.description: Research methods should be selected and combined by their strengths and limitations rather than treated as a universal best-to-worst hierarchy.
headings: Research methods are trade-offs, not a ranking

files.title: Research reveals complexity; segmentation organises it
files.description: Research exposes real variation in the market, and segmentation converts recurring patterns in that variation into a usable structure.
headings: Research reveals complexity; segmentation organises it

files.title: Resellers must retain independent price-setting
files.description: A supplier may recommend a resale price but must not turn that recommendation into a minimum through pressure, threats, supply withdrawal, or incentives.

files.title: Revealed choices can be more informative than stated explanations
files.description: When consumers cannot accurately explain their decision drivers, repeated choices and observed behaviour can reveal what influences them.
headings: Revealed choices can be more informative than stated explanations

files.title: Segment B2B markets at the account level
files.description: B2B segmentation should group qualifying organisations as accounts; decision makers are described later within selected target accounts.
headings: Segment B2B markets at the account level

files.title: Segment boundaries must preserve meaningful differences
files.description: Cut-off lines and group collapses should simplify the map only while distinctions that change treatment, behaviour, or positioning remain intact.
headings: Segment boundaries must preserve meaningful differences

files.title: Segment names should carry insight, not priority
files.description: Name segments with a memorable behaviour or defining insight, not with target priority, arbitrary themes, or derogatory labels.
headings: Segment names should carry insight, not priority

files.title: Segmentation is an option, not a default
files.description: A market may warrant targeted segmentation or mass marketing; the choice depends on whether useful, actionable differences justify selective treatment.
headings: Segmentation is an option, not a default

files.title: Segments must be coherent and large enough to serve
files.description: A useful segment groups customers who are meaningfully similar to one another, different from other groups, and numerous enough to serve economically.
headings: Segments must be coherent and large enough to serve

files.title: Settle strategy before selecting tactics
files.description: Tactical choices should implement an established strategy rather than determine it from the bottom up.

files.title: Strategic thinking requires protected time
files.description: Strategy requires deliberate time away from day-to-day execution so events do not dictate the plan.

files.title: Strategy requires choice and sacrifice
files.description: A strategy concentrates resources by deciding both what to pursue and what deliberately not to pursue.

files.title: Strategy should be disciplined while tactics remain agile
files.description: Execution should adapt to events while the governing strategy remains stable for its defined planning period.
headings: Strategy should be disciplined while tactics remain agile

files.title: Target portraits must come from evidence, not invention
files.description: A target portrait should synthesise qualitative and quantitative evidence about a chosen target rather than invent an idealised customer persona.
headings: Target portraits must come from evidence, not invention

files.title: Targeting breadth must balance reach, cost, and message advantage
files.description: Broad and focused targeting carry different benefits and costs; narrower reach must earn its added expense through greater relevance or value.
headings: Targeting breadth must balance reach, cost, and message advantage

files.title: Targeting, positioning, and objectives must cohere
files.description: Targeting begins strategy, but target, position, and objectives may need iterative adjustment as one choice changes another.
headings: Targeting, positioning, and objectives must cohere

files.title: Targeting requires a clear yes-or-no choice
files.description: Targeting should make explicit selections and rejections rather than disguise an all-market approach with priority rankings.
headings: Targeting requires a clear yes-or-no choice

files.title: The value of creative pre-testing depends on method and context
files.description: Creative pre-testing should be judged by how realistically and predictively it measures response, as well as by its value for refinement and stakeholder decisions.
headings: The value of creative pre-testing depends on method and context

files.title: Touchpoint priorities must be measured, not assumed
files.description: Organisations should use customer evidence to identify the breadth, importance, and performance of touchpoints rather than prioritising from internal opinion.
headings: Touchpoint priorities must be measured, not assumed

files.title: Touchpoints and funnels answer different questions
files.description: Funnels diagnose movement through a market for objective setting, while touchpoints examine an individual's continuing experience for product improvement.
headings: Touchpoints and funnels answer different questions

files.title: Triangulate secondary data without assuming it is correct
files.description: Multiple secondary sources can improve confidence, but pre-existing information still requires checks for reliability, timeliness, completeness, and access to underlying data.
headings: Triangulate secondary data without assuming it is correct

files.title: Underpricing can be harder to correct than overpricing
files.description: An initial price set too low can forgo profit and establish a low perceived-value position that is difficult to raise later.
headings: Underpricing can be harder to correct than overpricing

files.title: Understand customers in their real context
files.description: Customer understanding improves when marketers observe people in the settings where products, services, and decisions are actually experienced.
headings: Understand customers in their real context

files.title: Schemas
files.description: Data shapes a Framework or Playbook produces or consumes in the verified marketing knowledge base — never real client data.
